Subject: Re: Egress controls, KMS locality and subprocessors - technical summary

Hi Anna / Marissa,

Below is a short technical summary intended for contracting and security review. Happy to jump on a quick call if you want more detail.

1) Egress controls and routing model- Redwood assigns a region of origin for customer data at the tenant level (EU / US / APAC). By default, all inference requests for that tenant are routed to compute in the chosen region(s).

- In-region serving: production inference and persistent storage remain in-region.
- KV/prefix cache: cached artifacts are stored in-region; we use TTLs to limit surface area.
- Cross-region replication: asynchronous metadata replication (for monitoring/observability) is minimized and encrypted; we can disable non-essential replication on request.

2) Failover and temporary cross-region processing- We support contractually defined regional failover:

- Controlled failover: if capacity in-region is exhausted or there is a regional outage, requests may be routed to a designated secondary region under agreed conditions.
- Ephemeral processing: any cross-region handling is transient — the inference result is not stored outside the originating region except for customer-accepted logs/metrics.
- Quantitative cap: our standard offering limits involuntary cross-region routing to a fraction of requests during extreme events. For Acme we can propose a cap (e.g., <= 0.05% of total request volume per month) and a maximum outage-duration window per incident.

3) KMS and key locality- We offer two options:

A) Redwood-managed keys with regional locality: encryption keys and key material are stored within the tenant region (subject to supported cloud KMS availability).
B) Customer-managed keys (BYOK): you bring keys managed in your KMS (region of your choice). We support HSM-backed KMS and will never export key material from the region unless explicitly configured.

4) Auditability and logs- We can provide the following artifacts for contractual attachments:
- KMS key location attestations
- Access logs showing key usage with timestamps and region
- Per-tenant audit trail for any cross-region egress events (including reason and routing decision)

5) Subprocessors- Attached is a current extract of our subprocessor mapping (subprocessors_20251029.csv). We maintain a live list and can provide a signed appendix listing subprocessors per region for contract attachments.

Proposed contractual language (short form) to limit cross-region processing:
"Redwood will not process Customer Data outside the Customers designated region except: (a) as set forth in Section X (Regional Failover) upon the occurrence of a documented outage or capacity event; (b) for the limited purpose of temporary caching and monitoring as described in the Technical Summary. Any cross-region processing under (a) shall not exceed [CAP]% of the Customers monthly request volume without prior written consent, and Redwood shall notify Customer within 24 hours of any such event with an incident report."

(We left [CAP] for negotiation — we suggested 0.05% as a default for enterprise failover scenarios; this is flexible.)

Attachments: region-egress-technical-summary-20251030.pdf (technical appendix)

If you want the clause tightened to require written consent for any cross-region processing (i.e., CAP=0), we can prepare contract language and confirm operational feasibility for your scale.

-Rishi

Thanks — see below a proposed mutual action plan (MAP) and attached redline. Weve aimed for clarity on notice, CAP, and audit artifacts so procurement can move to PO.

MAP (proposed timelines):
1) Contract redline (you review): TODAY -> Acme returns comments by Wed 2025-11-05
2) Security attestation pack (KMS integration docs + key location evidence): Redwood to deliver by Fri 2025-11-07
3) Subprocessor appendix (signed): Redwood to provide current per-region appendix by Mon 2025-11-10
4) Procurement PO and billing setup: target Fri 2025-11-21

Key contractual proposals for Acme to consider:
- CAP: set to 0% for production tenant traffic; allow a separate onboarding window (first 14 days after initial rollout) where up to 0.1% involuntary cross-region routing may occur.
- Notice: Redwood will provide automated incident notification via the customer console and email; for EU-impacting incidents Redwood will also send a tailored incident summary within 1 hour of detection and a full incident report within 24 hours.
- BYOK: Redwood supports HSM-backed BYOK and will provide a technical integration packet; key material remains under the customer's KMS control and is never exported by Redwood unless the customer explicitly requests key export.
